items.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer mentions Jerry Jemmott as a bass player on a session with Gil Scott-Heron; the interviewee (Hubert Laws) does not mention Jemmott or indicate any personal or professional interaction with him.

ctx.x: Next one up, there’s another session with Gil Scott-Heron, called Free Will. Again, Bernard Purdie on that one, David Spinoza, Jerry Jemmott, bass player from Motown days. Then, right after that – this is March – then, after that – actually it’s the same day, because this is March 2nd, 1972. Then the next session is with Bobby Hutcherson, Natural Allusions, March 2nd and 3rd. So there you talk about going on your bike. But these were from – I’m not sure if you went on your bike back down to Englewood Cliffs, back…

No no. I would drive my car. I had a car. I always drove my car out to Englewood Cliffs, because I had – I told you, I had a nice garage where my building was, right there, covered garage. I’d just open it up. But I may have gone – I may have to use a car to go to that other session. It depends how much time I had between the two sessions.
